name: Coppertone sunscreen

lead: Coppertone is a U.S. sun care brand that began as a 1944 suntan lotion and became known for its girl-and-puppy advertising.
It is now mostly a sunscreen line, owned by Beiersdorf after a 2019 announced acquisition from Bayer.

paras: As a sunscreen brand it relies on UV filters; the sources reviewed do not list the filters used by specific products.
No brand-specific clinical safety studies were found. Early marketing emphasised tanning, and its history reflects changing sun-care norms.

lead: Coppertone is a U.S. sun care brand. According to Wikipedia, it traces to a suntan lotion developed by pharmacist Benjamin Green in 1944, and it is described as the leading U.S. sun care brand [1]. Its early marketing centred on tanning (slogan 'Tan, don't burn') rather than sunscreen as such [1].
Its best-known imagery is the 'Little Miss Coppertone' ad: a girl whose swimsuit is tugged by a puppy, exposing a tan line [1]. Few clinical studies concern the brand specifically.

paras: Green developed the lotion in 1944 to deepen tans. The original logo was a profile of an American Indian chief; in 1953 a Florida agency, Tally Embry Advertising, created the girl-and-puppy concept, and artist Joyce Ballantyne Brand redrew it in 1959 after a fire destroyed the original [1]. A mechanical Coppertone sign still stands in Miami Beach [1].

Plough acquired the brand in 1957; it passed to Schering-Plough in 1971, Merck in 2009 and Bayer in 2014, and in 2019 Beiersdorf announced it would acquire it [1]. Wikipedia also says a product originally made for the U.S. military was adapted for Coppertone in the early 1950s [2].
The line now consists mostly of sunscreens plus other skin care, and many products share a distinctive fragrance [1].

No studies found that evaluate Coppertone sunscreens' effects on skin cancer or sunburn in people. Related laboratory work includes a 1981 hairless-mouse study comparing protective factors across seven sunscreens [3], and a 2021 laboratory study that used Coppertone lotion as a base for botanical mosquito repellents, which concerned repellency rather than sun protection [4].

timeline.event: Benjamin Green develops the suntan lotion. [1]
Bayer acquires Merck's consumer business, including Coppertone. [1]
Beiersdorf announces plan to acquire Coppertone from Bayer. [1]
